title: staged-telemetry-driven-commit-agent-for-safe-optimize-autodeploy
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Build a staged commit agent (Commit Agent) that can safely apply Optimize batching/caching recommendations to customer configurations. The agent will combine simulated canary traffic, telemetry-based health gates, operator approval checkpoints, and automatic rollback policies to minimize risk when applying cost-saving config changes. It must produce auditable actions and integrate with Console rollouts and Redwood Optimize suggestion pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Commit Agent applies a suggestion to a 1% canary cohort automatically after passing simulation and telemetry checks
If key SLOs (99th latency, error-rate, model perplexity regression) exceed thresholds during any phase, the agent triggers immediate rollback and notifies on-call
Every applied change is logged with before/after config, rollout percent, decision rationale, and link to simulation report
Manual approval gates exist at 10% and 50% rollout steps and can be overridden only by a named operator with audit entry
Agent exposes a dry-run mode that produces a simulation report without changing live configs
Integration tests simulate a failing canary and verify automatic rollback path completes within 5 minutes
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Dry-run and simulation (0% prod) for 48h across representative traffic; Phase 1: 1% canary for 2 hours with full telemetry checks; Phase 2: 10% with operator approval and 24h observation; Phase 3: 50% with operator approval and automated kill-switch; Phase 4: 100% or gradual ramp to 100% after 72h stable. Each phase failure triggers immediate rollback to previous stable profile and creates a postmortem ticket.
telemetry_queries: sql:SELECT estimate, actual FROM inference_costs WHERE model_id = ? AND ts > now() - interval '1 day'
decisions: Use simulated canary (traffic replay) as first gate rather than immediate live shadow to reduce blast radius
Operator approvals required at mid-rollout thresholds to balance speed and human oversight
Implement signal-weighted scoring combining latency, error-rate, and eval regressions to decide automatic progression
Use Console audit log as single source-of-truth for applied commits and operator notes
updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed for traffic replay prototype against a synthetic workload; simulation produced false-positive variance that was traced to seed selection - fixed sampler.
2025-02-20: Integration contract agreed with Console team for rollout webhooks and approval callbacks; API shims spec'd.
2025-02-27: Telemetry gating RFC reviewed by SRE and Research; added model-output quality (eval) to gating signals.
2025-03-03: End-to-end staging test passed for dry-run + 1% canary. Observability hooks validated. Moving to extended canary.
2025-03-03: On-call playbook drafted and attached to PR; paging thresholds finalized with SRE
risks: False negatives in simulation could allow regressions to reach production
Overly conservative gates could prevent beneficial cost savings being realized
Operator fatigue if too many manual approvals are required
Complex rollback paths could leave partial config state across Dedicated and Private deployments
mitigation: Maintain conservative safety thresholds by default and expose tuning for customers
Provide rich simulation reports to reduce operator approval friction
Implement idempotent config commits and a strong transaction model for config patches
Add automated reconciliation job that verifies active config matches expected release manifest every 5 minutes
testing_notes: Create synthetic traffic profiles that mimic token-length distributions observed in production; include long-tail session tests
Introduce fault-injection scenarios (latency spike, model OOM, degraded KV cache) in staged canary to validate rollback
Write end-to-end harness that runs dry-run -> canary -> forced-failure -> rollback and asserts state consistency
related_customer_stories: Customer A: 20% token cost saving when caching prefix for search vertical; required staged rollout to limit latency impact
Customer B: Needed private deployment support for autodeploy approval due to compliance review
notes_for_ops: On-call should expect a single aggregated alert channel for Commit Agent failures. Runbooks: restart pipeline worker, revert using rollback API, open postmortem if >10% customers affected.
open_questions: Should we allow customers to opt-out of automatic progression entirely, defaulting to manual-only?
What SLA do we document for time-to-rollback in Dedicated vs Hosted environments?
How do we expose per-customer risk scores in Console without leaking telemetry from other tenants?
